   Business and Industry Commission /
  Green Vernon Commission Agenda Report

Meeting Date:  March 15, 2023
From:  Todd Dusenberry, General Manager of Public Utilities
Department:  Public Utilities
Submitted by:  Adriana Ramos, Administrative Analyst

Subject
Presentation on the Integrated Resource Plan Survey and Upcoming Outreach Efforts

Recommendation
No action required by the Commissions. This is a presentation only.

Background
The California Energy Commission (CEC) requires Publicly Owned Utilities, like Vernon Public
Utilities, to create an Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) every five years. IRPs describe how utilities
plan to meet their energy and capacity resource needs, policy goals, physical and operational
constraints, and other utility priorities, while maintaining competitive rates.

Public Utilities Code requires the CEC to review IRPs to ensure they meet various law policies
and regulations, including greenhouse gas emission reduction targets and renewable energy
procurement requirements. VPU completed its last IRP in 2018 and is currently in the process of
updating its plan. VPU is using the contracted services of Ascend Consulting Services (Ascend)
to assist in the IRP process. Together, VPU and Ascend will analyze the City’s electric demand
forecast, review the City’s existing and proposed energy resources and programs, examine the
City’s interconnections and distribution facilities, and assess renewable energy and Renewable
Portfolio Standard compliance requirements.

The IRP will provide a sustainable, comprehensive strategy to deliver reliable service, maintain
competitive and stable rates, and achieve environmental goals, the City wishes to engage its
stakeholders, like the Green Vernon Commission, BIC, Businesses, and residents to gauge
interest to obtain renewable sources in the utility’s portfolio.

VPU will provide a presentation that outlines its upcoming outreach efforts to help develop the
IRP, including the introduction of a survey to get feedback.
Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Presentation on the Integrated Resource Plan Survey and Upcoming
  Outreach Efforts
  Recommendation: No action required by the Commissions. This is a presentation
  only.

  Public Utilities Integrated Resources Manager Raufdeen presented the staff
  report.

  In response to Commissioner questions, Public Utilities Integrated Resources
  Manager Raufdeen stated the previous IRP was available on the City’s website.
  He discussed means of promoting the survey and efforts to include prospective
  stakeholders; renewable requirements and resources; efforts to meet the 2045
  California mandate; and State mandates for both public-owned and investor-
  owned utilities. He acknowledged the challenge of meeting State regulations while
  prioritizing reliability and low rates. He confirmed the IRP would model renewable
  options, and thus present the least cost gap necessary to achieve these goals. He
  stated plans for converting MGS to become a green asset would also be included
  in the IRP study. Public Utilities Business and Account Supervisor Serrano
  explained that businesses utilizing solar were based on NEM (Net Metering
  program), which prevented customers from over producing energy and thus could
  not assist with meeting renewable requirements.
